title: Kerr-Filtered Hybrid States from Double-Squeezed Tripartite Interactions
abstract: Multipartite interactions provide a unique route to generate hybrid quantum states, yet their intrinsically weak nonlinear coupling limits the controllable manipulation of the resulting correlations. Here we show that cooperative double squeezing and cavity Kerr nonlinearity together enable controllable engineering of Kerr-filtered hybrid states in a tripartite spin-photon-phonon system. Double squeezing exponentially enhances the spin-mediated photon-phonon pair-generation channel, whereas the Kerr interaction selectively reshapes the photonic component while maintaining the underlying tripartite conversion process. This mechanism reconstructs the composition of the hybrid excitation and gives rise to a fourfold phase-space manifold associated with spontaneous $Z_{2}^{(a)}\times Z_{2}^{(b)}$ parity breaking. Our results reveal a strategy for engineering hybrid quantum states by combining interaction amplification with mode-selective nonlinear filtering.
summary: This paper demonstrates a method to engineer complex hybrid quantum states in a spin-photon-phonon system by combining two effects: double squeezing, which enhances correlation generation, and cavity Kerr nonlinearity, which acts as a selective filter. This combination allows researchers to control the final composition of the quantum state, revealing rich superradiant phases and underlying symmetries.
main_problem: The paper addresses the limitation where the composition of a multipartite quantum state is intrinsically locked to the microscopic process generating its correlations, aiming to selectively reconfigure the state composition.
main_result: The combination of double squeezing and Kerr filtering enables the controllable engineering of Kerr-filtered hybrid quantum states, leading to distinct superradiant phases (SR I and SR II) characterized by a fourfold symmetry-related manifold.
method: The analysis uses Bogoliubov transformations, master equations for open systems, and mean-field approximations to study the ground-state phase diagram and phase-space structure.
model_or_system: The system is a tripartite spin-photon-phonon setup involving an alkaline-earth atom coupled to a cavity and trapped in a 1D harmonic trap. The dynamics are governed by a tripartite Hamiltonian modified by Kerr nonlinearity.
key_observables: Bosonic order parameters, Fock distributions ($P_c(n), P_p(n)$), subsystem von Neumann entropies, and the joint cavity-phonon Husimi-Q distribution.
important_parameters: Double squeezing strength, Kerr nonlinearity strength, and system decay rates ($\kappa_a, \kappa_b, \gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the Kerr nonlinearity selectively modifies the photonic component without disrupting the underlying tripartite conversion channel, and uses leading-order self-consistent approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ground-state phase diagram (N, WSR, SR I, SR II) and show the evolution of the joint Husimi-Q distribution, revealing the fourfold symmetry structure in the SR II regime.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the problem of state composition control, detailing the physical model and Hamiltonian, analyzing the interplay between squeezing and Kerr effects in the ground-state phase diagram, and finally examining the phase-space signatures and robustness against dissipation.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it combines multiple advanced topics in AMO physics: cavity QED (photon-matter coupling), quantum optics (squeezing, Kerr nonlinearity), and open quantum systems (dissipation), to achieve state engineering.

Figure 6. Cutoﬀdependence of the ground-state Fock dis- tributions in the Kerr-free limit (K0 = 0). The cavity and phonon distributions are shown for increasing Hilbert-space truncations: (a) Na = Nb = 60, (b) Na = Nb = 100, (c) Na = Nb = 160, and (d) Na = Nb = 200. Parameters are ra = rb = 0.2 and ˜g1/ ˜∆a = 2. The probability maxima continuously shift toward the cutoﬀboundary as the trunca- tion is increased, indicating the absence of a converged ﬁnite- occupation ground state in the Kerr-free model. This cutoﬀ dependence reveals the unbounded growth of hybrid photon– phonon excitations when no nonlinear saturation mechanism is present.
